segments.t: Right in the middle of Barinov and Elena's romantic moment, the front door opens and Lyova walks in with his mother after missing their train. When Vera Ivanovna introduces herself as Lyova's mother rather than Viktor Petrovich's, a humiliated Elena storms out.
А мы, вы знаете, вот смотрим телевизор.
Простите, я что-то не очень понимаю.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Oh, excuse me, you are not alone.' The meaning hinges on 'oh no' working together with 'one' in spoken Russian.
А мы, вы знаете, вот смотрим телевизор.
'You see, we were just watching television.' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'television' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Lyova answers right away.
'I asked my son to change the lightbulb.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'to replace' without extra filler words.
'We were on our way to the train station.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'railway station'.
Простите, я что-то не очень понимаю.
'Excuse me, I do not quite understand.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'forgive' and finishing on 'understand'. Elena answers right away.
'Whose mother are you?' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'mum' in spoken Russian.
'Is she your mother?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'this' and finishing on 'mum'.
'I am Lyova's mother, Vera Ivanovna.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'Ivanovna' without extra filler words. Lyova answers right away.
'Very pleased to meet you.' The grammar packs 'very' and 'to meet' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I can explain everything.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'I will explain' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'No, thank you.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'there is no' and finishing on 'to thank'. Elena answers right away.
'Maybe some other time.' Elena brings out the contrast between 'another' and 'time' in a few short words.
'Thank you very much.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'to thank' before landing on 'you'. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
А мы, вы знаете, вот смотрим телевизор.
Простите, я что-то не очень понимаю.
When you watch Scene 20 of Episode 15, listen out for the exchange around vera ivanovna's return — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
